The suggested fix matches the codebase's own established pattern (Checklists.tsx:276 Badge uses role="img" aria-label; Checklists.tsx:69 names its role="group"), so it stands as-is.

title: No h1, most views have no headings, and heading levels are inconsistent across tabs
description: The app title "SnowRaven" is styled <span>s in a <div> (App.tsx:570-580) — no h1 and no banner landmark. Settings, Life List, Species Detail, and Map Explorer contain no heading elements at all (section titles like "Appearance"/"Map Overlays" are styled divs), so SR heading navigation lands on nothing in four major views. Where headings do exist they are inconsistent: ListComparer.tsx:184 and ChecklistComparer.tsx:340 use h1 inside tab content while Checklists.tsx:522, BirdingStats.tsx:424 and NamedBirds.tsx:128 use h2; SetupRequired.tsx:31 (the empty state of 8 tabs) styles its title as a div. Additionally the main nav loses its landmark: role="tablist" on the <nav> (TabNav.tsx:105-108) overrides the navigation role, and in dropdown mode there is no nav element at all.
fix: Make the app title an h1 inside a <header>; give every tab view an h2 and section cards h3 (Settings/LifeList/SpeciesDetail/MapExplorer sidebar sections); make SetupRequired's title an h2; demote the comparer h1s to h2.

verdict.reasoning: All claims check out: the title is styled spans in a div (App.tsx:570-580, no h1/header element); grep shows zero heading elements in Settings, LifeList, SpeciesDetail, MapExplorer and SetupRequired (title is a styled div, SetupRequired.tsx:31); ListComparer:184/ChecklistComparer:340 use h1 in tab content while Checklists:522/BirdingStats:424/NamedBirds:128 use h2; TabNav.tsx:105-108 puts role="tablist" on the <nav> (killing the navigation landmark) and the dropdown variant renders no nav at all. Heading navigation is a primary SR strategy and four major views expose nothing, so this is genuinely user-impacting at 1.3.1 Level A; moderate is the right tier since tablist/main/contentinfo landmarks still give a navigation path.
verdict.fixNote: The suggested heading plan is sound (h1 title in <header>, h2 per view incl. SetupRequired, h3 section cards — statsPrimitives.tsx already uses h3 for stats cards, so follow that pattern), but it omits the landmark half of its own description: also move role="tablist" off the <nav> in TabNav.tsx onto an inner div so the navigation landmark survives, and wrap the dropdown-mode trigger+listbox in the same <nav aria-label="Main navigation">.

title: Disclosed chart-bar-label exception verified — but it understates the dark-theme failures (down to 1.29:1) and a working fix already exists in-code
description: ACCESSIBILITY.md's known exception ('a few dense data-visualization labels (percentage figures printed inside saturated chart bars) do not yet meet AA in every case') is accurate in direction but materially understates scope. Computed: LIGHT — white on --sr-graph-audio 2.15:1 (protocol bar), white on --sr-chart-slate 2.56:1, white on --sr-graph-photo 3.68:1, white on --sr-graph-video 4.23:1. DARK — --sr-text on --sr-chart-blue-light 1.29:1 (comment/species-notes bars, BirdingStats.tsx:1384/1405), white on graph-audio 1.44:1, white on --sr-accent 1.92:1 (hardcoded '#fff' at protocol bar :1181), white on graph-photo 2.54:1, white on chart-slate 2.56:1, --sr-text on chart-slate 2.33:1 (:1361), white on chart-blue-dark 3.68:1 (:1125). In dark mode it is most in-bar labels, not 'a few'. Notably, line 1358 already uses var(--sr-on-accent) which passes in BOTH themes (4.52/7.75) — the failures are the literal '#fff' and var(--sr-text) usages that don't adapt.
fix: Replace literal '#fff' bar-label colors with per-fill adaptive tokens (the existing --sr-on-accent pattern), or render the percentage outside/beside the segment when the segment color can't carry AA text; then tighten the ACCESSIBILITY.md wording to match whatever remains.

verdict.reasoning: Independently recomputed every cited pair with my own WCAG relative-luminance implementation; all match (dark --sr-text on --sr-chart-blue-light = 1.29:1 at lines 1384/1405, white on dark graph-audio 1.44, white on dark accent 1.92 via the hardcoded '#fff' at 1181, dark text-on-slate 2.33 at 1361, white on dark chart-blue-dark 3.68 at 1125), and line 1358's --sr-on-accent does pass both themes (4.52/7.75) proving the fix pattern exists in-code. Labels are 11-12px weight-600, so the 4.5:1 normal-text threshold applies — in dark mode most in-bar labels fail, some catastrophically, which materially exceeds the 'a few cases' wording in ACCESSIBILITY.md line 31. Confirmed at moderate: the percentages are supplemental (raw counts appear in the adjacent header text), but 1.29:1 is effectively invisible text.

title: Dark theme: map pin tokens are lightened 'for dark backgrounds' but draw on the always-light Positron basemap (1.69–2.25:1)
description: There is no dark basemap variant (lib/mapStyle.ts tunes Positron only; no theme branch), yet the dark-theme --sr-map-* tokens lighten the pin colors: visited/heat pins #34D399 vs Positron land (~#F2F0EB) = 1.69:1, personal #E0A060 = 1.97:1, unvisited #7BA7C9 = 2.25:1 (light theme passes: 3.66–3.97:1). The GL circle/teardrop sprites read these tokens at runtime (map/SightingMarkers.tsx:80, lib/mapPins.ts, HotspotMarkers sprites), so switching the app to dark mode makes the primary map markers fainter against the unchanged light tiles. White glyphs inside the dark-theme teardrops also drop below 3:1 (star on #E0A060 = 2.24:1, dots on #7BA7C9 = 2.56:1). Mitigation: the sidebar in-view lists duplicate marker info, which keeps this from serious.
fix: Anchor the on-map pin tokens to the basemap, not the app theme (keep the light-theme values in dark mode, or add a dark halo/outline to the GL sprites); keep the lightened values only for sidebar legend dots that actually sit on dark surfaces.

verdict.reasoning: Verified the mechanism end-to-end: lib/mapStyle.ts has no dark basemap variant (Positron only), SightingMarkers.tsx reads --sr-map-visited via useCssToken at runtime (theme-reactive per the data-theme MutationObserver contract), and my recomputation matches exactly — dark tokens #34D399/#E0A060/#7BA7C9 hit 1.69/1.97/2.25:1 on ~#F2F0EB land, with white teardrop glyphs at 2.24/2.56; the pin strokes are hardcoded white (SightingMarkers.tsx:160, mapPins.ts:133) so they add no edge contrast on light tiles. One inaccuracy: light theme does NOT fully pass — --sr-map-personal #C9842A is only 2.70:1 on the land tint, so the personal pin fails 1.4.11 in both themes. ACCESSIBILITY.md documents the sidebar keyboard path to markers but not marker contrast, so not disclosed; the sidebar mitigation keeps moderate the right severity.
verdict.fixNote: Add dedicated basemap-anchored pin tokens (e.g. --sr-map-pin-*) defined with the SAME values in both :root and [data-theme="dark"] for the GL circle layer and sprite bakes, keeping the existing --sr-map-* for sidebar legend/list dots on app surfaces. Note 'keep the light-theme values' alone is insufficient: light --sr-map-personal #C9842A is itself 2.70:1 on the land tint, so pair the shared pin tokens with a dark stroke ring — replace the hardcoded #ffffff circle-stroke-color (SightingMarkers.tsx:160) and sprite strokeStyle '#fff' (mapPins.ts:133) with a dark outline to supply the 3:1 boundary against light tiles.

title: Light theme: accent-colored text marginally fails on tinted/page backgrounds (4.03–4.32:1)
description: Light --sr-accent #2D8653 passes on white surfaces (4.52:1) but fails where it is used on anything tinted: on --sr-accent-bg = 4.03:1 — the app-wide active-state pattern (ghost buttons, active filter pills, the tab dropdown's selected option TabNav.tsx:309-314, SpeciesPanel count badge :44-45; background:'var(--sr-accent-bg)' + accent text appears in 14 files); on --sr-bg = 4.32:1 — the active tab label (tab bar sits directly on the page background, App.tsx:583) and the footer 'Up to date' status (App.tsx:1154); on --sr-surface-subtle = 4.11:1. Dark theme passes everywhere (7.75–10.35:1).
fix: In light theme use --sr-accent-strong (#1A5C38; 7.12:1 on accent-bg, ~6.7:1 on bg) for accent-as-TEXT on tinted/page backgrounds, keeping --sr-accent for fills, borders and focus rings; or darken light --sr-accent to ~#27764A so it clears 4.5:1 on --sr-accent-bg.

verdict.reasoning: Independent WCAG relative-luminance math reproduces every reported ratio exactly: light #2D8653 is 4.03:1 on --sr-accent-bg #E8F5EE, 4.32:1 on --sr-bg #F9FAFB, 4.11:1 on --sr-surface-subtle #F4F4F5 (4.52:1 on white passes; dark theme passes at 7.75-10.35). The pairs genuinely co-occur — dropdown selected option (TabNav 309-314), SpeciesPanel count badge (11px accent text on accent-bg), active tab label over the body's --sr-bg background, footer 'Up to date' span — all normal-size text requiring 4.5:1, and 24 files reference --sr-accent-bg. ACCESSIBILITY.md claims AA for primary interface colors with only chart-bar labels excepted, so this is a real undisclosed AA failure; the suggested --sr-accent-strong fix is convention-compliant (token defined in both themes; verified 7.12:1 on accent-bg, 7.64:1 on bg) and the alternative #27764A verifies at 4.96/5.32/5.56.

title: Light theme: error text on error background is just below AA (4.41:1)
description: --sr-error #DC2626 on --sr-error-bg #FEF2F2 computes to 4.41:1 — marginally under 4.5:1 — and this pair styles every error banner and the 'negative' filter pill state: Checklists.tsx:236/488, LifeList.tsx:108/384, BreedingCodeList.tsx:196, Settings.tsx:304/480, ChecklistComparer.tsx:374, NamedBirds.tsx:108, WeatherTidePanel.tsx:186, SpeciesDetail.tsx:430, DropZone.tsx error text. Dark theme passes (7.07:1). Error on plain surface also passes (4.83:1), so only the tinted-banner pair needs a nudge.
fix: Darken light --sr-error slightly (e.g. #D31F1F ≈ 4.8:1 on #FEF2F2) or introduce an --sr-error-text token used on --sr-error-bg; one token edit in globals.css fixes all listed locations.

verdict.reasoning: Verified the pair co-occurs (Checklists.tsx:236 TriPill 'no' state and :488 error banner, plus the other listed files) and re-computed the ratio: #DC2626 on #FEF2F2 = 4.415:1, a genuine but marginal AA miss at 13px text; dark theme (7.07:1) and plain-surface (4.83:1) pass as the finding states. The 0.085 shortfall is perceptually negligible and light-theme-only, so 'moderate' overstates user impact — this is a compliance nudge, not a barrier; downgrading to minor. The fix is validated (#D31F1F = 4.82:1 on #FEF2F2, 5.27:1 on white) and convention-compliant as a single light-theme token edit in globals.css.

title: Light theme: muted text on tinted surfaces falls just under AA (4.27–4.40:1)
description: --sr-text-muted #71717A passes on white (4.83:1) but not on the tinted surfaces it is commonly paired with in light theme: on --sr-surface-subtle = 4.40:1 (inactive segmented-control labels in MapSidebarUI SegControl, the basemap switcher buttons in globals.css:246, the missing-media badges in the target popup TargetMarkers.tsx:92, numerous chips); on --sr-quote-bg = 4.27:1 (Named Birds comment block); on --sr-accent-bg = 4.31:1 (secondary text inside selected rows, e.g. the location line of a selected Nearest Targets row, MapExplorer.tsx:1306+1317). Dark theme passes all three (5.27–5.82:1).
fix: Darken light --sr-text-muted to ~#6B6B74 (≈4.6:1 on #F4F4F5) — a single token change; verify it still reads as 'muted' next to --sr-text.

verdict.reasoning: Independent WCAG math confirms the ratios: #71717A is 4.397:1 on #F4F4F5, 4.268:1 on #EFF1F3, and 4.310:1 on #E8F5EE (dark theme passes 5.27-5.82), and the surface-subtle and accent-bg pairings genuinely co-occur at small text sizes (SegControl inactive labels MapSidebarUI.tsx:13+24, basemap switcher globals.css:234/246, TargetMarkers.tsx:92 badges, selected-row secondary text MapSidebarUI.tsx:96+109 and MapExplorer.tsx:1306+1317); these are enabled controls, so the inactive-component exemption does not apply. One cited pairing is wrong: the quote-bg comment blocks (NamedBirdRow.tsx:110, Checklists.tsx:350-351) use full-contrast --sr-text, not muted, so that instance never occurs — but the finding stands on the other two surfaces. The proposed #6B6B74 verifies as passing everywhere (4.66-4.80 on the tinted surfaces, 5.28 on white), and changing only the :root value is convention-clean since the token already exists in both themes; not covered by ACCESSIBILITY.md's chart-bar-label exception.

title: ToggleSwitch off-state track is nearly invisible in light theme (1.48:1)
description: The off-state track uses --sr-gray-400 (#D4D4D8): 1.48:1 against the white button surface AND 1.48:1 against the white knob, so the knob position — the visual state indicator of every 'merge subspecies' / 'show spuh' / 'hide weather' switch — is barely discernible in light theme (the on state passes: accent track 4.52:1 vs surface). Dark theme: track vs surface 2.29:1 (also <3:1) though knob-vs-track passes (7.73:1). aria-checked is correct for AT, but the sighted off/on distinction fails non-text contrast.
fix: Darken the light off-track (e.g. #8E8E96 ≈ 3.1:1 on white and vs the white knob) and lighten the dark off-track (e.g. #6E6E78), or add a 1px --sr-border-medium-darkened outline to the track and knob.

verdict.reasoning: Independently recomputed all ratios from globals.css tokens and they match exactly: light off-track #D4D4D8 is 1.48:1 vs both the white surface and the white knob (knob position imperceptible), on-track 4.52:1, dark track 2.29:1 vs surface with knob-vs-track 7.73:1. ACCESSIBILITY.md claims form controls meet AA contrast and discloses only chart-bar labels, so this is not a known exception. Moderate is right: a genuine 1.4.11 failure on a widely-used control, but state remains inferable from green-present/absent (state-vs-state 3.06:1) and aria-checked is correct for AT.
verdict.fixNote: The suggested hexes verify (#8E8E96 = 3.25:1 on white; #6E6E78 = 3.51:1 vs dark surface, 5.04:1 vs white knob), but '--sr-border-medium-darkened' does not exist and hardcoded hexes in the component would violate the --sr-* token rule. Since --sr-gray-400 has no other consumers, either retune --sr-gray-400 to #8E8E96 (:root) / #6E6E78 ([data-theme="dark"]) in frontend/src/globals.css, or — cleaner, since #8E8E96 would be oddly dark for a 'gray-400' slot — add a dedicated --sr-toggle-off-track token in BOTH themes and reference it at ToggleSwitch.tsx:27. Also update the ACCESSIBILITY.md contrast claim if the fix doesn't ship immediately.

title: Form-control borders are far below non-text contrast (1.19–1.34:1)
description: --sr-border (#E4E4E7 light / #27272A dark) is the only boundary cue on text inputs, selects, date inputs and unselected pills throughout the app (SELECT_STYLE here; the same '1px/1.5px solid var(--sr-border)' pattern on inputs in MapExplorer, Checklists, LifeList, Settings, SpeciesDetail). Computed: 1.27:1 light / 1.19:1 dark vs surface, 1.21:1 / 1.34:1 vs page bg; even --sr-border-medium is 1.73:1 light / 1.70:1 dark. Inputs whose extent is identified only by this border fail 1.4.11; the focus ring fixes it only once focused.
fix: Introduce an --sr-border-input token at ≥3:1 vs surface (≈#949499 light, ≈#5F5F66 dark) for form-control boundaries, or give inputs a contrasting filled background (--sr-surface-subtle is itself only 1.07:1 vs surface, so the border route is simpler).

verdict.reasoning: Re-computed all ratios and they match: --sr-border vs surface is 1.27:1 light / 1.19:1 dark (1.21/1.34 vs page bg), --sr-border-medium 1.73/1.70 — the borders are near-invisible. But the W3C Understanding of 1.4.11 does not require a visible boundary when the control is otherwise identifiable, and every cited control carries a placeholder ('Search by place name', 'Paste your API key', 'e.g. 37.8275') and/or a visible label, and SELECT_STYLE selects show a ~4.7:1 chevron glyph — so this is a genuine low-vision usability weakness, not a clear normative AA failure. Confirmed as a worthwhile polish fix at minor severity rather than moderate.
verdict.fixNote: The --sr-border-input token approach is right (define in both :root and [data-theme="dark"]), but the suggested dark value #5F5F66 is only 2.80:1 vs --sr-surface #18181B — below the fix's own 3:1 target. Use ~#6B6B73 (3.35:1) or #707078 (3.61:1) for dark; light #949499 passes at 3.02:1 but only barely, so a slightly darker value gives margin.

title: Hardcoded milestone-chip and rank-icon colors below AA (2.76–4.16:1), bypassing the token system
description: The Firsts & Milestones chips hardcode hex colors (also violating the project's tokens-only rule): the tier-1 date link #5EA07C on #E8F5EE = 2.76:1 (10px text), tier-1 number #2D8653 on #E8F5EE = 4.03:1, tier-2 date #3E7A56 on #D8EDE4 = 4.16:1 (tier-3/4 pass: 4.92–6.37:1). These values are identical in both themes since the chips don't adapt. Separately, RankIcon (statsPrimitives.tsx:97-98) prints white 10px-bold rank numbers on hardcoded #3B82F6 = 3.68:1 (the #2D8653 circle squeaks by at 4.52:1).
fix: Move the milestone palette into --sr-* tokens and darken the failing fg values (date ≥ #43755C on #E8F5EE; num → --sr-accent-strong); for RankIcon use --sr-chart-blue-dark (#1D4ED8, 6.70:1 under white) as the square fill.

verdict.reasoning: Hardcoded hexes verified at BirdingStats.tsx:671-677 and statsPrimitives.tsx:95-98 (violating the CLAUDE.md tokens-only rule), and my recomputation matches: tier-1 date 2.76:1 and tier-2 date 4.16:1 at 10px (need 4.5), RankIcon white-on-#3B82F6 3.68:1 at 10px bold (need 4.5). One overstatement: the tier-1 threshold number is 1.25rem/700 = 20px bold = WCAG large text, so its 4.03:1 PASSES at the 3:1 large-text threshold — the real failures are the two date links and the RankIcon square. Still a fair moderate: real sub-AA text plus a standing-convention violation.
verdict.fixNote: Tokenize the milestone palette into --sr-milestone-* tokens defined in BOTH :root and [data-theme="dark"] (globals.css), darkening only the failing date colors (tier-1 date >= #43755C on #E8F5EE = 4.76:1, tier-2 date similarly); the tier-1 number (20px bold = large text) already passes at 4.03:1 >= 3:1 and needs no change. Do NOT use var(--sr-chart-blue-dark) for the RankIcon square as suggested — it resolves to #3B82F6 in the dark theme, which is 3.68:1 under the white 10px-bold rank text and still fails; instead add a dedicated token (e.g. --sr-rank-square: #1D4ED8 in both themes, 6.70:1 under white) and use var(--sr-accent... ) tokens for the circle.

title: 'Personal Location' popup badge fails in light theme (2.90:1)
description: The hotspot popup's 'Personal Location' badge sets --sr-map-personal (#C9842A) text on --sr-is-target-bg (#FFF7ED): 2.90:1 in light theme at 11px/600 (dark passes, 8.38:1). The pin color token was designed as a map fill, not a text color.
fix: Use --sr-is-target-text (#C2410C, 4.88:1 on that bg) or --sr-warning for the badge text in light theme.

verdict.reasoning: Independently recomputed: #C9842A (--sr-map-personal) on #FFF7ED (--sr-is-target-bg) = 2.90:1 in light theme at 11px/600 — small text, fails the 4.5:1 AA minimum exactly as reported; dark theme (#E0A060 on #1C0F00) = 8.38:1, passes. HotspotMarkers.tsx:156 matches the finding, and the badge is the popup's only textual indicator that the pin is a personal location, so it is meaningful text — moderate stands. Not disclosed: ACCESSIBILITY.md affirmatively claims map popups meet AA and lists only chart-bar percentage labels as the known exception.
verdict.fixNote: Swap color: 'var(--sr-map-personal)' for 'var(--sr-is-target-text)' unconditionally — no light-theme branch needed, since the token is theme-scoped (4.88:1 light, 8.30:1 dark, both pass) and --sr-is-target-bg + --sr-is-target-text is already the codebase's badge pairing (LifeList.tsx:529).

title: DropZone error state's border and icon are nearly invisible (1.74–1.90:1)
description: In the error state the drop zone's border and upload icon switch to --sr-error-muted (#FCA5A5 light): 1.74:1 against the --sr-error-bg fill and 1.90:1 against the surrounding surface, so the state-change boundary/icon fails non-text contrast (dark: icon vs surface 2.74:1; vs error-bg 3.02:1 passes). The role=alert error text is present, but it itself is the marginal 4.41:1 light error-on-error-bg pair reported separately.
fix: Use --sr-error (#DC2626) for the error-state border and icon — 4.41:1 vs error-bg and 4.83:1 vs surface, comfortably over the 3:1 non-text bar.

verdict.reasoning: DropZone.tsx lines 39-43 and 108 set the error-state border and icon to --sr-error-muted on --sr-error-bg; my own WCAG luminance math reproduces every reported ratio (light 1.74:1 vs error-bg, 1.90:1 vs white surface; dark 2.74:1 vs surface, 3.02:1 vs error-bg), confirming a 1.4.11 failure in light theme and a marginal dark theme. The role=alert text partially conveys the state, so moderate is the right severity. The suggested var(--sr-error) fix is verified in both themes (4.41/4.83:1 light, 7.07/6.40:1 dark) and follows the --sr-* token convention; note it must be applied at both line 40 (border) and line 108 (icon).

title: ACCESSIBILITY.md contrast claim is broader than the computed reality
description: The published statement says text, buttons, links, map popups and form controls 'meet the WCAG 2.1 AA contrast standard (4.5:1) in both the light and dark themes', with chart-bar labels as the only known exception. Computed counterexamples outside that exception: light-theme active pills/links on tinted backgrounds 4.03–4.41:1 (accent-on-accent-bg, error-on-error-bg, active tab on page bg), --sr-text-disabled used on content at 2.29–2.56:1, dark-theme target chips at 1.52–1.92:1, dark-theme breeding pills at 1.97–2.94:1, and form-control borders at 1.19–1.27:1 (non-text). The repo treats this file as a published statement whose claims must be true; today it overstates. (Verified-true parts: the tier-1 badge example, the recency-dot hidden labels, the text-footer/sci-name token fixes, focus-ring contrast, and the dark-mode popup theming.)
fix: Either fix the token-level failures in this report (most are 1-line token edits) and keep the claim, or temporarily widen the known-exceptions paragraph to honestly cover active-state tints in light theme and chip/pill labels in dark theme.

verdict.reasoning: Recomputed all cited ratios independently and each one holds with co-occurring real UI: light accent-on-accent-bg 4.03 / error-on-error-bg 4.41 (LifeList.tsx:107-108 active pills) / active tab on bg 4.32 (TabNav.tsx:94); --sr-text-disabled 2.29-2.57 on non-disabled content (Settings.tsx:240/376 sublabels); dark target chips 1.52/1.92 (white text hardcoded in lib/mapExplorerFormat.ts:61-62); dark breeding pills 1.97-2.94 after alpha-blending the 0.08 tints (BreedingCodeList.tsx:43-60); borders 1.19-1.27. ACCESSIBILITY.md:31 claims AA in both themes with only the chart-bar-label exception, so the published statement is overstated — and CLAUDE.md explicitly requires this file's claims to stay true. The only stated exception does not cover any of these, so alreadyDisclosed is false.
verdict.fixNote: The two-option fix is sound, with one correction: the dark-theme target-chip failure is not a token edit — lib/mapExplorerFormat.ts hardcodes text: 'white' (itself against the no-hardcoded-colors convention). Fix it like the existing old-tier pattern: add --sr-map-target-fresh-text / --sr-map-target-mid-text tokens to BOTH :root and [data-theme="dark"] in globals.css and reference them, mirroring --sr-map-target-old-text. The breeding-pill fix likewise needs the dark-theme tier text colors lightened (or pill text switched to --sr-text) rather than tint-alpha tweaks, since the 0.08 tint barely moves the blended background. Any token change must land in both theme blocks per convention; ACCESSIBILITY.md edits alone need no version bump.

title: Media count badges in checklist comparer use aria-label on a generic <span> — info silently lost to screen readers
description: MediaIcons renders per-species photo/audio/video presence as lucide SVG icons inside a plain <span aria-label={`${n} ${label}`}>. ARIA prohibits naming on role=generic, so most browser/SR pairs ignore the aria-label, and the SVGs themselves have no text alternative — the media information (which types exist and counts) is conveyed to sighted users only. The same file's Checklists tab equivalent (Checklists.tsx:276 Badge) does this correctly with role="img", and ChecklistBadges.tsx is correct too — this one component missed the pattern.
fix: Add role="img" to the span (matching the Badge pattern in Checklists.tsx:276) so the aria-label is exposed: <span role="img" aria-label={`${n} ${label}`} ...>.

verdict.reasoning: ChecklistComparer.tsx:57 puts aria-label on a bare span (role generic, where ARIA prohibits naming, so exposure is unreliable) wrapping lucide SVGs that carry no text alternative; no other text path in SideCell conveys media presence or counts. The repo's own correct pattern exists at Checklists.tsx:275 (Badge with role="img" aria-label), confirming this component missed it. Moderate is right: real informational content (a headline comparer data point) with no reliable SR exposure, but not a control or blocker.
verdict.fixNote: The suggested role="img" fix is correct and matches the in-repo Badge pattern; while there, reuse the already-built pluralized text for the name so SR output matches the tooltip: <span role="img" aria-label={`${n} ${label.toLowerCase()}${n > 1 ? 's' : ''}`}> (the current aria-label would announce '2 Photo').

title: Repeated "↗" checklist links named only by the arrow glyph
wcag: 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context) A / 2.4.6 Headings and Labels AA
description: Three Statistics sections render external eBird checklist links whose only content is the character "↗" with title="Open checklist": the effort superlative cards (line 1332), single-checklist-bird chips (line 1564), and one-and-done bird chips (line 1589). The accessible name is computed from content, so every one of these (potentially dozens in the chip lists) is announced as "north east arrow, link" or skipped entirely depending on SR symbol verbosity — identical and non-descriptive. title only provides a description, not the name, when content exists.
fix: Add aria-label, e.g. aria-label={`Open eBird checklist ${bird.submissionId} for ${bird.name} (opens in a new tab)`}, mirroring NamedBirdRow.tsx:94 which already does this correctly, and mark the glyph aria-hidden.

verdict.reasoning: All three sites verified (BirdingStats.tsx:1332, 1564, 1589): anchor content is solely the ↗ character with title="Open checklist", so per accname computation the name is the glyph (title only supplies the description when content exists) — dozens of identical, non-descriptive links in the chip lists, indistinguishable in a screen-reader links list. The cited in-repo precedent is real: NamedBirdRow.tsx:94 already uses aria-label={`Open eBird checklist ${s.submissionId} (opens in a new tab)`} with an aria-hidden icon. Moderate is fair (2.4.4 in-context is arguable for the chip-adjacent bird name, but the repeated-identical-name failure mode is genuine) and the suggested fix matches the codebase pattern exactly.

title: Missing-media type icons in Media Targets popup and marker chips have no text alternative anywhere
description: The whole point of a media target is which media types (photo/audio/video) the user is missing, but that information is conveyed exclusively by unnamed inline SVGs: in the target popup (TargetMarkers.tsx:91-97, bare <svg> per missing type, no aria-hidden, no label), in the on-map chip labels (TargetMarkers.tsx:62, MEDIA_ICONS SVG strings injected via dangerouslySetInnerHTML), and the keyboard-accessible "Nearest Targets" sidebar rows (MapExplorer.tsx:~1315-1318) show only name/location/distance — they omit missing types entirely. A screen-reader user can find a target but never learn which media it is missing. This also weakens the ACCESSIBILITY.md claim that icon-only information "carries a hidden text label so it is never lost to a screen reader."
fix: In the popup, give each type span role="img" aria-label={`Missing ${t.toLowerCase()}`} (or append sr-only text) and aria-hidden the SVGs; add the missing types as text (visible or sr-only) to the Nearest Targets sidebar rows so the keyboard/SR path carries the full information.

verdict.reasoning: Verified all three cited surfaces: popup spans (TargetMarkers.tsx:91-97) hold bare unnamed SVGs with no role/aria-label/sr-only text, chip labels inject raw MEDIA_ICONS SVG strings via dangerouslySetInnerHTML (line 62, mapExplorerFormat.ts:30-34) with no ARIA, and the Nearest Targets sidebar rows (MapExplorer.tsx:1315-1319) render only name/location/distance — missingTypes never appears as text on any keyboard/SR path. The type-filter pills filter the set but don't convey per-target info, so the feature's core information is icon-only, contradicting ACCESSIBILITY.md line 19's hidden-label claim. Moderate is the right severity: SR users can reach targets but lose the missing-media detail.
verdict.fixNote: The suggested fix is right; extend it slightly: also add aria-hidden="true" into the three MEDIA_ICONS SVG strings in lib/mapExplorerFormat.ts so browse-mode screen readers don't hit unnamed images on the on-map chips, and for the sidebar rows reuse the existing sr-only span pattern already used for the recency dot at MapExplorer.tsx:1311-1313 (e.g. Missing photo, audio).

title: DOM map markers (Species Detail / Named Birds pins, target chips, Statistics rank pins) are unnamed, role-less click targets invisible to AT
wcag: 1.1.1 Non-text Content A / 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value A
description: ACCESSIBILITY.md documents sidebar-list alternatives for the Map Explorer's GPU canvas markers, but the DOM <Marker> maps have no equivalent treatment: SightingsMap.tsx:55-58 renders each pin as a clickable <div> containing an innerHTML SVG with no role, name, or tabindex; TargetMarkers.tsx:69-74 does the same for target chips; BirdingStats.tsx:863-872 for the Statistics RankIcon pins (statsPrimitives.tsx:92-101, an unnamed SVG). Screen-reader and keyboard users cannot perceive or activate any of these markers or reach their popups. Impact is moderated because equivalent data exists in adjacent text on most surfaces (Named Birds rows list every sighting date/location/checklist; Species Detail has Top Locations and per-sighting lists; Statistics has top-location tables), but the popup-only details (e.g. per-coordinate date groupings) have no named path.
fix: Make the Marker child a real button: role="button", tabIndex=0, aria-label like `${locName ?? coordinate}, ${sightings.length} sightings` with Enter/Space handling — or explicitly scope the ACCESSIBILITY.md marker claim and guarantee a text equivalent exists beside every DOM-marker map.

verdict.reasoning: The literal 'no role, name' claim is partly wrong — maplibre 5.24's Marker.addTo() (src/ui/marker.ts:340-348) stamps every marker wrapper with role='button' and default aria-label='Map marker' — but the substantive 1.1.1 failure stands: all pins announce identically with no location/count, are not focusable (tabindex comes only from the unused setPopup path), and the popup-only per-coordinate details have no named path. The cited mitigations are real (BirdingStats pins duplicate the adjacent 'Top locations by checklists/species' lists; NamedBirdRow lists every checklist link; TargetMarkers has the Nearest Targets sidebar), so moderate is the right severity. ACCESSIBILITY.md's marker claim is Map Explorer-only and does not disclose this.
verdict.fixNote: Correction to the finding's mechanism: the markers are not role-less/invisible — maplibre already applies role='button' + a generic identical aria-label ('Map marker') to the wrapper, so the defect is a non-descriptive name plus no focusability. Fix by giving each pin a descriptive per-pin name: either set it on the wrapper via the Marker ref (marker.getElement().setAttribute('aria-label', `${locName ?? coord}, ${n} sightings`) plus tabindex='0' — maplibre preserves a pre-set label), or render a real <button aria-label=...> child and demote the wrapper to role='presentation' via the ref to avoid nested-button announcements. The finding's hand-rolled role='button'/tabIndex/Enter-Space div is workable but creates button-inside-button nesting and re-implements what a native <button> gives for free.

title: Placeholder-only (or format-only) accessible names on text inputs; Map Explorer From/To dates are indistinguishable
wcag: 2.4.6 Headings and Labels AA / 1.3.1 Info and Relationships A
description: Several inputs have no label or aria-label, so the accessible name falls back to the placeholder. Worst case: the Map Explorer date-range inputs (MapExplorer.tsx:862,864) both have placeholder "YYYY-MM-DD" — a SR user hears the format string twice with nothing distinguishing From vs To (the visible "Date Range" SidebarLabel is not programmatically associated). Same pattern: MapExplorer.tsx:84 (place search), 689/691 (Latitude/Longitude), 1182 (target species search); Settings.tsx:1216/1228/1240 map-default inputs, whose visible "Latitude"/"Longitude"/"Radius (mi)" labels are unassociated <div>s so the computed name is "e.g. 37.8275"; SpeciesDetail.tsx:1268 and MediaCommentsSection.tsx:70 comment filters (placeholder is at least descriptive there, but disappears once text is typed for sighted users). Contrast: Checklists.tsx:655/663 date inputs do it right with aria-label="From date"/"To date".
fix: Add aria-label to each (e.g. "From date (YYYY-MM-DD)" / "To date (YYYY-MM-DD)", "Latitude", "Longitude", "Search by place name"), or associate the existing visible labels via htmlFor/id.

verdict.reasoning: Verified every cited input: MapExplorer 862/864 are both placeholder="YYYY-MM-DD" with the 'Date Range' SidebarLabel an unassociated div, so From and To compute identical accessible names; 84, 689/691, 1182, Settings 1216/1228/1240 (visible Latitude/Longitude/Radius labels are plain divs), SpeciesDetail 1268, and MediaCommentsSection 70 all have placeholder-only names. Checklists.tsx 655/663 confirmed as the in-house aria-label="From date"/"To date" pattern the fix mirrors. Moderate is right — placeholders provide a partial name fallback, but the indistinguishable date pair is a genuine 2.4.6/1.3.1 failure.

title: Placeholder is the only label on search/filter, coordinate, and API-key text inputs
description: These text inputs have no label or aria-label; their only identification is the placeholder, which disappears as soon as the user types (and browsers' placeholder→accessible-name fallback is a last resort, not a reliable label). Locations: MediaCommentsSection.tsx:66-70 ('Filter media comments…'); Checklists.tsx:161-165 (shared CommentSearchBox, placeholders 'Filter checklist comments…' / 'Filter species comments…' at :544/:555); SpeciesDetail.tsx:1264-1268 ('Filter comments…'); MapExplorer.tsx:82-84 ('Search by place name'), :689/:691 (Latitude/Longitude number inputs — after entry a sighted user sees two bare numbers with nothing saying which is which), :1182-1184 ('Search species…'); Settings.tsx:424-428 (API key entry, 'Paste your API key' — the row label at :352 is an unassociated <div>). Impact is worst for low-vision and cognitive users mid-entry, and for the lat/lng pair where the only differentiator vanishes.
fix: Add aria-label to each input (e.g. aria-label="Filter media comments", aria-label="Latitude", aria-label="eBird API key") while keeping the placeholder as a hint; for the Map Explorer lat/lng pair, prefer small visible labels like the Settings map-defaults section already has.

verdict.reasoning: Read every cited input: MediaCommentsSection.tsx:66-79, the shared CommentSearchBox in Checklists.tsx:161-175 (both instantiations), SpeciesDetail.tsx:1264-1277, MapExplorer.tsx:82-89/:689-692/:1182-1185, and Settings.tsx:424-440 — none has an aria-label, aria-labelledby, or associated <label>; the placeholder is the only identification, and the Settings row label is an unassociated <div>. ACCESSIBILITY.md's only disclosed exception is chart-bar contrast, so this is undisclosed. Moderate is correct: placeholder fallback usually yields *some* accessible name, but it vanishes on input (worst for the bare lat/lng number pair, which affects sighted users too) — a fair 3.3.2 AA failure, not serious, not pedantry.
verdict.fixNote: The suggested aria-labels are right and match the file-local convention (Checklists.tsx already puts aria-label on its Protocol/County selects and From/To date inputs; MapExplorer/Settings use aria-label heavily elsewhere). One refinement: CommentSearchBox is a shared component, so add a single aria-label derived from its existing title/placeholder prop (e.g. aria-label={placeholder.replace(/…$/, '')}) — one change covers both Checklists instances. For Settings, derive it from the row's label prop (aria-label={`${label} API key value`} or similar) rather than a hardcoded string, since the component renders multiple key rows.

title: Atlas block popups are pointer-only — no keyboard route to open them
description: Atlas block info popups open exclusively via a MapLibre map.on('click','sr-atlas-fill') handler on the GL fill layer (AtlasLayer.tsx:109-132). There is no sidebar list, search, or other focusable path to a block, so the popup's content — block name, the eBird atlas portal link, and 'Highest breeding code … N of your breeding records in this block' — is unreachable without a pointer. The breeding data shown in the popup is not surfaced anywhere else in the app (the sidebar legend only explains tier colors). The popup JSX itself is fine (escaped, keeps the default labeled close button), but keyboard users can never open it.
fix: When shading is on, add a focusable 'Shaded blocks in view' sidebar list (mirroring InViewMarkerList — blocksInBounds already provides viewport-scoped blocks and breedingByBlock the per-block data) whose rows open the same popup; or expose a block search/jump input. Cap + hint like the other lists.

verdict.reasoning: Verified the cited handler (AtlasLayer.tsx:109-132) is the sole path to setSel, and grep confirms BlockBreeding/breedingByBlock data is surfaced nowhere else in the app, so the popup content is genuinely pointer-only. The suggested fix matches existing conventions (InViewMarkerList in map/MapSidebarUI.tsx, blocksInBounds viewport scoping, cap+hint pattern) and correctly notes only shaded blocks need listing. Not disclosed in ACCESSIBILITY.md; moderate severity appropriate. (Duplicate of finding 20.)

title: Map sidebar filter inputs rely on placeholders for their accessible names; date inputs are named 'YYYY-MM-DD'
wcag: 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value A (also 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions A)
description: The Map Explorer sidebar inputs have no <label>, aria-label, or aria-labelledby — the SidebarLabel headings are unassociated styled divs. Accessible names therefore fall back to placeholders: the two Date Range inputs (MapExplorer.tsx:862-865) both compute to the meaningless, identical name "YYYY-MM-DD" (a screen-reader user cannot tell From from To, or that they are date filters at all); Latitude/Longitude (:689-692), "Search by place name" (:86), and "Search species…" (:1182) are intelligible but vanish once a value is typed. The adjacent Search button (:90-103) has only a title attribute for its name.
fix: Add aria-label="Date from (YYYY-MM-DD)" / "Date to (YYYY-MM-DD)" (and aria-labels echoing the other placeholders), or give SidebarLabel an id and reference it via aria-labelledby plus a per-field qualifier. Give the search icon button aria-label="Search". (Flagging here because these gate the map experience; may overlap with a forms-dimension audit.)

verdict.reasoning: Verified at MapExplorer.tsx:862-865 the two date inputs are type=text with identical YYYY-MM-DD placeholders and no label/aria-label/aria-labelledby, and SidebarLabel (MapSidebarUI.tsx) is an unassociated styled div; lat/lng (:689-692), place search (:84), species search (:1182) are placeholder-named and the search button (:93) is title-only. One nuance: per HTML-AAM a placeholder remains the computed accessible name even after a value is typed (the 'vanish' is visual-only, a 3.3.2 issue), but the identical meaningless names on the two date fields are a genuine 4.1.2/3.3.2 failure that gates the map filters. Severity moderate is appropriate and the aria-label fix matches existing codebase patterns (e.g. the heatmap slider's aria-label at :930).

title: Map chrome text inherits MapLibre's fixed `font: 12px/20px Helvetica` — does not scale with the in-app Text Size control
description:
maplibre-gl.css (imported at SnowMap.tsx:7) sets `.maplibregl-map{font:12px/20px Helvetica Neue,…}`. The app's `.maplibregl-popup-content` override in globals.css:568 themes colors but sets no font-size or family, so any map-rendered text without an explicit rem size stays at a hard 12px Helvetica regardless of the Text Size setting. Affected: (1) the AtlasLayer block popup title — `
{sel.name}
` at AtlasLayer.tsx:213 and the linked variant at :208-211 have no fontSize; (2) the attribution credits on every map (SnowMap.tsx:121 `attributionControl={{ compact: true }}` — provider links render at fixed 12px when expanded); (3) the AtlasLayer popup's default close button (it is the only popup that doesn't pass `closeButton={false}`, so users get maplibre's small fixed-size '×' — also a WCAG 2.2 2.5.8 Target Size concern). This matters more here than in a typical web app: ACCESSIBILITY.md:37 states the Text Size control is "especially useful in the desktop app, which has no browser zoom of its own", so on desktop this text is genuinely un-resizable. All other popups (SightingMarkers, HotspotMarkers, TargetMarkers, SightingsMap, the BirdingStats geo popup) set explicit rem sizes and are fine.
fix: In globals.css extend the existing popup override: `.maplibregl-popup-content { font-size: 0.8125rem; font-family: var(--font-sans); }` and add `.maplibregl-ctrl-attrib { font-size: 0.6875rem; }`; give the AtlasLayer block-name elements an explicit rem fontSize; pass `closeButton={false}` on the AtlasLayer popup for consistency with the other four popups (its onClose path already exists).

verdict.reasoning: Every claim checks out: maplibre-gl.css sets .maplibregl-map{font:12px/20px Helvetica Neue,...}, the globals.css:568 popup override adds no font-size/family, the AtlasLayer block name (:208-213) has no fontSize, .maplibregl-ctrl-attrib inherits the fixed 12px, and the Text Size control scales only rem text via html{font-size:calc(100% * var(--sr-text-scale))} (globals.css:378). On desktop — which ACCESSIBILITY.md:37 itself says has no browser zoom — this text is un-resizable, a genuine 1.4.4 failure there (web is saved by browser zoom); at 200% the popup title would render smaller than its own muted secondary text. AtlasLayer is indeed the only popup of six without closeButton={false}, but that part of the fix is wrong (see fixNote).
verdict.fixNote: The CSS parts are right: extend the existing globals.css override with `.maplibregl-popup-content { font-size: 0.8125rem; font-family: var(--font-sans); }` and add `.maplibregl-ctrl-attrib { font-size: 0.6875rem; }`, and give the AtlasLayer block-name elements an explicit rem fontSize (e.g. 0.8125rem). But do NOT pass closeButton={false} on the AtlasLayer popup: it also sets closeOnClick={false}, so the default close button is its only dismiss affordance and its only keyboard-operable control — removing it would strand the popup open and worsen 2.1.1. Instead keep the button and size it via the existing .maplibregl-popup-close-button override (e.g. add `font-size: 1rem; padding: 2px 8px;`), which also addresses the 2.5.8 target-size concern.

title: Fixed-pixel text geometry in Statistics overlaps or clips at 200% text scale (pattern, multiple locations)
wcag: 1.4.4 Resize Text AA (clipping cases also 1.4.12 Text Spacing AA)
description: One repeating pattern: rem-sized text placed in fixed-pixel boxes that don't grow with the text. (1) BarRow (statsPrimitives.tsx:59-75): label column `width: labelWidth, flexShrink: 0` and value column `width: pctOf ? 68 : 40`, no overflow handling — at 200% scale, labels ("Jan" at labelWidth=28: BirdingStats.tsx:754,794,829; "SnowRaven weather" at 120: BirdingStats.tsx:1425-1429; MediaStatsSections.tsx:180-182,294) and values like "1,234 (56%)" are ~2× wider than their boxes and overlap the adjacent bar graphic. (2) Stacked-bar % labels inside fixed-height `overflow: hidden` segments — BirdingStats.tsx:1122-1133 and 1173-1185 (height 32, fits 200%) but the protocol sub-bars at 1151-1158 are `height: 20` with 0.625rem labels: at 200% the 20px glyphs (30px line box) clip vertically; same construction in the media bars at 1356, 1380, 1401. (3) Hard-ellipsized name columns `width: 100`/`width: 96` + nowrap+hidden (BirdingStats.tsx:953, 984, 1028, 1057) — county/species names truncate to a few characters at 200% with only a mouse-only `title` as recovery. (4) Donut center captions absolutely centered in fixed 120/132px charts — BirdingStats.tsx:764-769, 804-807 and MediaStatsSections.tsx:58-61 — at 200% the caption (e.g. "September" ≈140px wide, or a 1.25rem count) spills across the donut ring on both sides. Screen-reader users are unaffected (the role="img" aria-labels carry the data); this degrades the visual rendering for sighted low-vision users at 150-200%.
fix: Convert the fixed widths to rem (e.g. labelWidth 28→'2.5rem', value column '4.5rem') or `minWidth` + `flex-basis`; change the sub-bar `height: 20` to `minHeight: 20` (the % label centers itself, the bar just grows); for the donut captions either size the chart in rem or cap centerValue/centerLabel with a clamp().

verdict.reasoning: All four cited sub-patterns exist in current code (BarRow px label/value columns at statsPrimitives.tsx:59-75 with labelWidth 28/48/120/150 at the cited consumer lines; height-20 overflow-hidden sub-bars at BirdingStats.tsx:1151-1158; 100/96px ellipsized county/state columns at 953/984/1028/1057, counties lacking even a title; fixed 120/132px donut charts with absolutely-centered captions). The app's Text Size control doubles the root font-size via --sr-text-scale while these px boxes stay fixed, so single-word labels overlap the bars, sub-bar labels clip at the 20px clip edge, names truncate to a few characters, and donut captions spill across the ring at 200% — and ACCESSIBILITY.md affirmatively claims 1.4.4 is met 'without clipping content', so this contradicts the published statement rather than being disclosed. Two specifics are overstated (the '1,234 (56%)' values wrap onto a second line rather than overlapping since rows use minHeight, and the height-32 media bars at 1356/1380/1401 fit at 200%), but the pattern and moderate severity stand.
verdict.fixNote: Direction is right, but: BarRow's labelWidth prop is typed `number`, so convert inside the component (width: `${labelWidth / 16}rem`, value column `pctOf ? '4.25rem' : '2.5rem'`) so no call sites change; `height: 20` → `minHeight: 20` on the sub-bars is correct as suggested; recharts PieChart width/height are px numbers so the donut can't be 'sized in rem' — instead give the centered caption maxWidth: '100%' with padding and ellipsis/wrap (or compute the chart px size from the live root font-size); and for the county columns at BirdingStats.tsx:953/984 either add the missing title attribute or replace the hard ellipsis with a rem minWidth that lets names wrap.

title: List Comparer summary bars and result panels don't reflow at 320px — labels truncate to identical text
description: Both comparer results screens use rigid column counts with no narrow-width collapse. The five-cell summary (`gridTemplateColumns: 'repeat(5, 1fr)'` — ResultsView.tsx:111 and ChecklistComparer.tsx:281) gives each cell ~58px at 320px; the 0.625rem uppercase labels are `whiteSpace: nowrap; overflow: hidden; textOverflow: ellipsis` (ResultsView.tsx:165-173, ChecklistComparer.tsx:478), so "Checklist A" and "Checklist B" (and "<name> total" pairs) ellipsize to identical strings — the numbers become indistinguishable at that width. Below them, ResultsView.tsx:129 `repeat(3, 1fr)` species panels and ChecklistComparer.tsx:310 `1fr 1fr` A-only/B-only panels never stack, leaving ~90-140px columns where species names wrap to 4+ lines. Nothing scrolls two-dimensionally and the panel headers repeat the counts, so it is degraded rather than lost — but the summary labels' ambiguity is a concrete information loss at 320px.
fix: Use `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(7rem, 1fr))` for the stat bars (cells wrap to two rows on narrow screens), and collapse the panel grids to one column under 640px (reuse the `.sr-two-col` media-query pattern from globals.css:601).

verdict.reasoning: Verified all cited lines: ResultsView.tsx:111 `repeat(5, 1fr)` with nowrap/ellipsis 0.625rem labels (165-176), :129 `repeat(3, 1fr)` panels, and the ChecklistComparer twins (281, 310, ~479) — all inline styles with zero responsive handling (no matchMedia, no media-query class) anywhere in ResultsView/ListComparer/ChecklistComparer. At 320px each stat cell is ~55-64px with 40px horizontal padding, leaving ~15-24px for the label (1-3 chars + ellipsis): 'Checklist A'/'Checklist B' and filename-derived labels (eBird exports share the 'MyEBirdData' prefix) truncate to identical strings — concrete information loss under SC 1.4.10, though the both/A-only/B-only counts are duplicated in the panel headers so only the two totals become truly ambiguous. Moderate is the right severity: real AA failure at 320px/400% zoom, but degraded rather than blocking.
verdict.fixNote: The stats-bar half of the fix is sound (rem-based `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(7rem, 1fr))` inline also scales with the in-app Text Size control). The panel half won't work as written: the grids' `gridTemplateColumns` are inline styles, and a media-query class rule cannot override an inline declaration — move the grid definition into a class (as SpeciesDetail.tsx:802 uses `className="sr-two-col"` with no inline grid). ResultsView's panel grid is 3 columns, so `.sr-two-col` isn't directly reusable: either add an `.sr-compare-panels { grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr) }` base rule with a `1fr` override in the existing `@media (max-width: 640px)` block in globals.css (the ChecklistComparer's 1fr-1fr grid CAN reuse `.sr-two-col` directly), or skip media queries entirely with inline `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(14rem, 1fr))`. Also note ACCESSIBILITY.md line 39 currently claims narrow-window reflow 'without clipping content' — it should be corrected or the fix shipped to keep that published statement true.

title: 'Nearest Targets' list is not scoped to the map view and does not update on pan/zoom, contrary to the statement
description: ACCESSIBILITY.md says the Media Targets mode's 'Nearest Targets' list 'works the same way' as the in-view lists and then asserts 'These lists are scoped to the current map view and update as you pan or zoom (very dense views are capped, with a "zoom in to narrow the list" hint).' The keyboard path itself is real (each row has a focusable, aria-labelled locate button at lines 1320-1333 that opens the same popup and pans). But `nearest10` (lines 453-461) is computed as the 10 closest pins to the SEARCH CENTER lat/lng inputs — it ignores `mapBounds`, never reacts to panning or zooming, and has no over-cap hint. Only the 'Sightings in view' and 'Hotspots in view' lists (markersInView + mapBounds, cap 200, MapSidebarUI.tsx:118-121) match the published description. A screen-reader user following the statement would expect the targets keyboard list to track the viewport; it doesn't.
fix: Either scope the targets list with markersInView(displayedTargetPins, mapBounds) like the other two lists, or correct ACCESSIBILITY.md to say the targets list is the 10 nearest to the search center.

verdict.reasoning: nearest10 (MapExplorer.tsx:453-461) is sorted by distance from the lat/lng search-center inputs with deps [displayedTargetPins, lat, lng] — it never reads mapBounds, never reacts to pan/zoom, and has no over-cap hint — while ACCESSIBILITY.md line 13 explicitly includes the Nearest Targets list in 'These lists are scoped to the current map view and update as you pan or zoom'. The gap is functional, not just a claims bug: target chips are DOM divs with onClick but no tabIndex (TargetMarkers.tsx), so targets beyond the 10 nearest to the center have no keyboard path at all while mouse users can click any chip. Moderate is fair (false published assistive-behavior claim plus a real 2.1.1 gap).
verdict.fixNote: If scoping to the viewport, reuse the existing pattern rather than patching nearest10: derive markersInView(displayedTargetPins, mapBounds) and render through the shared InViewMarkerList (MapSidebarUI.tsx) like sightingsInView/hotspotsInView, which gives the cap + 'zoom in to narrow the list' hint for free. Otherwise the one-line ACCESSIBILITY.md correction ('the targets list shows the 10 nearest the search center') is the cheaper honest fix.

title: Tab Layout reordering is mouse/touch-only with no keyboard alternative — the statement's keyboard section discloses no exceptions
wcag: 2.1.1 Keyboard A (also WCAG 2.2 2.5.7 Dragging Movements AA)
description: Settings → Tab Layout reorders tabs exclusively via HTML5 drag-and-drop on the <li> rows; the 'drag handle' is a non-focusable plain <div> carrying an aria-label (which is also invalid ARIA on a generic div — it won't be announced), and there is no keyboard mechanism (no move-up/move-down buttons, no arrow-key handling). The app itself admits this in an sr-only note at Settings.tsx:699 ('Keyboard reordering is not supported in this version'), and ACCESSIBILITY.md's 'Nearly all of SnowRaven is reachable and operable with the keyboard alone' hedge technically covers it — but the Keyboard Navigation section enumerates zero exceptions, so a reader has no way to learn this feature is keyboard-inaccessible. Show/hide toggles are keyboard-accessible; ordering is not achievable at all without a pointer, which is a hard 2.1.1 failure for that function (and a 2.5.7 Dragging Movements failure under WCAG 2.2).
fix: Add keyboard reordering (focusable handle button with ArrowUp/ArrowDown + aria-live position announcements, or per-row Move up/Move down buttons), and until then name this exception explicitly in ACCESSIBILITY.md's keyboard section.

verdict.reasoning: Both halves check out: (a) reordering is pointer-only — DnD on the <li>, unfocusable handle div with an invalid aria-label, no keyboard mechanism in the file — and (b) ACCESSIBILITY.md's Keyboard Navigation section enumerates only the map-marker caveat and never names this exception, so the 'Nearly all' hedge gives readers no way to learn ordering is keyboard-inaccessible. The sr-only in-app note (line 699) is disclosure to SR users but not in the published statement, so alreadyDisclosed stays false. Moderate is fair for the claims-dimension framing (the underlying 2.1.1 failure is index 3's serious finding); the fix — keyboard reorder, or naming the exception in ACCESSIBILITY.md until then — is correct.

title: Closing the Help overlay drops focus to <body> instead of returning to the Help button
description: HelpDocs correctly focuses its Close button on open and traps Tab, but onClose (Close button or Escape) simply unmounts the overlay (App.tsx:1203-1205 just sets helpOpen false) — focus falls to document.body and the keyboard user restarts from the top of the page. The Map Explorer filter sidebar (filtersButtonRef refocus) and the TabNav dropdown (close(true)) both restore focus correctly; HelpDocs is the inconsistent one. It can be opened from three places (footer, Welcome screen, Settings), so the opener should be remembered.
fix: Capture document.activeElement when the overlay mounts and restore focus to it in a cleanup effect (covers all three openers without prop plumbing).

verdict.reasoning: This is the same defect as index 27 (exact duplicate, different cited line): App.tsx:1203-1205 just sets helpOpen false, no capture/restore code exists, and focus verifiably falls to <body>; the contrast with the map filter sidebar's correct refocus is accurate. Confirmed, but minor understates it — a keyboard user re-Tabs from the document top after every Help close, and the identical finding at index 27 is rated moderate, so aligned to moderate. Should be merged with index 27 as one finding.
verdict.fixNote: Same fix as index 27: a mount-time effect in HelpDocs declared before the closeRef-focus effect, capturing document.activeElement and refocusing it in the cleanup — covers all three openers without prop plumbing.

title: DropZone inline `outline: 'none'` defeats the global keyboard focus ring
description: The DropZone (role="button", tabIndex=0 — keyboard activation itself works) sets outline: 'none' in its inline style. Inline styles override the stylesheet's [role="button"]:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--sr-accent) } rule (globals.css:546-551, no !important), leaving only the rule's faint 12%-alpha box-shadow glow as the focus indicator; the border/background highlight is driven by mouse-only isHovered state. Keyboard users on the List Comparer get an almost invisible cue on the primary upload control. (Reported here because it directly degrades keyboard operation of an otherwise-correct widget; full focus-visible sweep belongs to that dimension.)
fix: Delete the inline outline: 'none' (the global :focus-visible ring only shows for keyboard focus, so the mouse aesthetics are unaffected), or mirror the isDragging accent border on :focus-visible.

verdict.reasoning: Line 69's inline outline:'none' overrides globals.css:542-551's [role="button"]:focus-visible / [tabindex]:focus-visible ring (no !important), leaving only the rule's rgba(45,134,83,0.12) box-shadow (~1.05:1 over the light surface, effectively invisible), and the component has no focus-driven styling of its own — isHovered is mouse-only. This directly contradicts ACCESSIBILITY.md's claim that every focused control shows a clear green outline, so it is not a disclosed exception. An effectively absent focus indicator on the List Comparer's two upload controls is a real 2.4.7 AA failure, understated at minor; the suggested fix (delete the inline outline:'none') is correct and safe since :focus-visible does not fire on mouse interaction.

title: WCAG 2.2 deltas: 14×14 favicon link targets and sticky-header focus obscuring
description: Forward-looking 2.2 items. (a) Target size: the eBird / Birds of the World favicon links rendered beside nearly every bird name are 14×14px, placed directly adjacent to each other — below the 24×24 minimum with no qualifying spacing exception; they are the most frequently repeated small target in the app. The Species Detail combobox chevron (SpeciesDetail.tsx:521, ~16px <span>) is also undersized but pointer-redundant. Most other small controls measured are compliant (close 26×26, eye 28×28, locate 26×26, FABs 36×36). (b) 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured: LifeListTable's sticky header row (position: sticky, top: 0 — LifeListTable.tsx:182-187) can fully cover row links (BirdName, ML catalog) when Shift+Tab scrolls a focused element up under it; same risk for BreedingCodeTable's sticky first column (line 128).
fix: Give the favicon anchors padding to reach a ≥24×24 hit area (visual size can stay 14px). For sticky tables, add scroll-padding-top equal to the header height on the scroll container so focused elements land below the sticky header.

verdict.reasoning: Verified: each favicon anchor's hit area is the 14x14 .sr-favicon-slot (globals.css:285) with no padding and a 5px gap, so centers are 19px apart and the 2.5.8 spacing exception fails; SpeciesLinks is composed into the app-wide BirdName, so the targets repeat everywhere. The 2.4.11 half is real but narrower than stated: LifeListTable's sticky header only engages in wideMode (the default-mode overflowX:auto wrapper becomes the scrollport and never scrolls vertically, so the header never sticks), while BreedingCodeTable's sticky 220px first column does engage and can cover the tabIndex=0 sortable column headers. Fairly flagged as forward-looking 2.2 deltas at minor; ACCESSIBILITY.md discloses neither.
verdict.fixNote: Favicons: add padding (e.g. 5px) on the anchors or .sr-favicon-slot, offset with negative margin to preserve dense-row layout, keeping the img at 14px. Sticky tables: scroll-padding-top must go on the ACTUAL scrolling element — for LifeListTable that is the document (html), not the table wrapper (the wrapper is only a horizontal scrollport, and in wideMode the header sticks to the viewport; scroll-padding-top on the wrapper would be a no-op). For BreedingCodeTable's sticky column the analog is scroll-padding-left: 220px on the overflowX:auto wrapper div.

title: Tablist lacks Home/End keys (APG completeness)
wcag: 2.1.1 Keyboard A (advisory — APG tabs pattern; no AA failure)
description: The desktop tab bar implements roving tabindex with ArrowLeft/ArrowRight + wrap (TabNav.tsx:109-123) but not Home/End to jump to the first/last tab, which the WAI-ARIA APG tabs pattern recommends (the collapsed dropdown DOES implement Home/End at lines 197-204, so the two modes are inconsistent). With 10+ tabs this is several extra keystrokes, not a barrier — forward-looking polish only.
fix: Add Home → items[0] and End → items[items.length-1] cases to the tablist onKeyDown, mirroring the dropdown's handling.

verdict.reasoning: TabBar's tablist onKeyDown (TabNav.tsx:109-123) handles only ArrowLeft/ArrowRight while the collapsed dropdown implements Home/End (lines 197-204), confirming both the gap and the cross-mode inconsistency. The finding correctly self-classifies as advisory APG polish with no AA failure (Home/End are optional in the APG tabs pattern, and arrow wrapping caps traversal at ~half the tab count), so minor is the right severity. The suggested fix mirrors an existing in-file pattern and is sound.

title: Map Explorer Filters accordion button lacks aria-expanded
description: The collapsible filter panel toggle in the sightings sidebar (button at :836, panel collapsed via max-height 0) exposes no expanded/collapsed state — the only cue is the rotated chevron. Every other disclosure in the app does carry aria-expanded (NamedBirdRow.tsx:36, ChecklistComparer.tsx:76/:440, TabNav.tsx:234).
fix: Add aria-expanded={filterOpen} (and optionally aria-controls) to the Filters button.

verdict.reasoning: The Filters disclosure button (MapExplorer.tsx:835-847) carries no aria-expanded; the only state cue is the rotated ChevronDown, and the panel collapses via maxHeight 0. Verified the cited convention claim: NamedBirdRow.tsx:36, ChecklistComparer.tsx:76 and :440, and TabNav.tsx:234 all set aria-expanded on their disclosures, so this is an isolated omission. Minor is right and the suggested one-attribute fix (aria-expanded={filterOpen}, optionally aria-controls) is correct and conventional.

title: Comment-count live regions announce on every keystroke
description: CommentSearchBox's match count (N comments, used by both the Checklist Comments and Species Comments sections) recomputes from the filter input on every keystroke, so a screen reader queues an "N comments" announcement per character typed, competing with character echo. The count announcement itself is good 4.1.3 practice — it just needs to settle.
fix: Debounce the text feeding the live region (~400-500 ms after typing pauses) while leaving the visible count immediate.

verdict.reasoning: Checklists.tsx:177 puts aria-live="polite" on the count span, and matches recomputes synchronously from the filter input (useMemo on filter, set in onChange), so every count-changing keystroke mutates the live region and queues an announcement over character echo — used by both comment sections. Slight overstatement ('every keystroke' is really 'every keystroke that changes the count') but substantively correct, and minor is the right severity. ACCESSIBILITY.md mentions polite count regions as a feature, not this chattiness as a known issue, so not already disclosed.
verdict.fixNote: The visible count and the live region are the same span, so a naive debounce would also lag the visible count. Split them: keep the existing visible span immediate but add aria-hidden, and render a visually-hidden sibling with aria-live="polite" fed by a ~400-500 ms debounced copy of the count text (debounced state via useEffect + setTimeout keyed on matches.length). Apply the same pattern to the line 668 checklist-count region, which has the same shape (though it is mostly click-driven, the date inputs can also type-churn it).

title: Comparison-mode switch uses tablist/tab roles without panels or arrow-key support
description: The Life Lists / Checklists mode switch is role="tablist" + role="tab" aria-selected, but there is no aria-controls, no role="tabpanel" for the swapped content, no roving tabindex, and no arrow-key handling — SR users are told they're in a tab widget whose conventions (arrows move, panel follows) don't hold. Inside the app shell's real tab system, this also nests tab semantics within a tabpanel.
fix: Either complete the pattern (ids + aria-controls + tabpanel + roving tabindex + arrows) or simplify to a role="group" of aria-pressed buttons like SortSeg.

verdict.reasoning: Verified at ListComparer.tsx:150-165: role=tablist/tab with aria-selected but no aria-controls, no tabpanel on the swapped content (line 168), both tabs tabIndex={0} (no roving), and no onKeyDown anywhere in the file. The nesting claim also holds — App.tsx mounts ListComparer inside the id=panel-comparer role=tabpanel. Keyboard operation still works via Tab+Enter on the real buttons, so minor is the correct severity; ACCESSIBILITY.md does not disclose this (it asserts the main tab bar follows the standard arrow-key pattern), and the suggested SortSeg-style role=group/aria-pressed fix matches the existing convention in Checklists.tsx.

title: TabDropdown listbox misuses aria-activedescendant and trigger lacks aria-controls
description: The dropdown menu manages focus by moving DOM focus to the option buttons (roving), yet the listbox container also sets aria-activedescendant — on an element that itself never receives focus (no tabindex), where the attribute has no effect, and pointing at the SELECTED tab rather than the focused option. All options are also tabIndex={0} (the pattern expects -1 with the container or roving single stop), and the trigger (:233) has aria-haspopup/aria-expanded but no aria-controls referencing the listbox. Functionally usable (DOM focus carries the announcements) but the ARIA contradicts the actual focus model.
fix: Remove aria-activedescendant (DOM focus already tracks the active option), set option tabIndex={-1}, give the listbox an id, and add aria-controls to the trigger.

verdict.reasoning: All claims verify in current code: line 269 sets aria-activedescendant={`tab-${activeTab}`} on a listbox div that never receives focus (no tabindex) and points at the selected rather than focused option, options are tabIndex={0} (line 300) despite roving DOM focus, and the trigger (lines 229-237) lacks aria-controls (the listbox also has no id to reference). The component is functionally usable since DOM focus carries announcements, so minor is the correct severity for this ARIA-contradicts-focus-model issue. The suggested fix (drop activedescendant, tabIndex={-1} on options, listbox id + trigger aria-controls) is correct — programmatic .focus() works on tabindex=-1 elements, so the existing focusItem logic is unaffected.

title: Species selector chevron is a click-only unnamed <span>
description: The open/close chevron beside the species combobox input is a <span onClick> with no role, no accessible name, and no keyboard access. The function is redundantly available (focusing the input opens the list, Escape closes), so impact is low, but it's an interactive element invisible to AT and unreachable by keyboard.
fix: Either mark it decorative (aria-hidden, remove onClick — the input already toggles) or make it a real button with aria-label="Toggle species list" and tabIndex={-1}.

verdict.reasoning: Verified at SpeciesDetail.tsx:521-531 — a <span onClick={() => setDropdownOpen(o => !o)}> with no role, no accessible name, no tabIndex, no key handler, and notably no aria-hidden either, so AT perceives a mystery element while keyboard users cannot reach it. Minor is correct since the function is fully redundant (input focus opens, Escape/Tab closes). The proposed fix (aria-hidden decorative, or a tabIndex={-1} button with aria-label per the APG combobox pattern) is right; note this duplicates finding 84.

title: role="status" loading indicators mount already containing their text (announcement unreliable)
description: Loading/status chips are conditionally rendered elements that carry role="status" AND their message in the same insertion: TabLoading (App.tsx:125), tide states (App.tsx:837-845), MapExplorer loading chip (:1437), BirdingStats (:464, :883), AtlasLayer (:230), WeatherTidePanel (:165-235). Live regions must exist before their content changes; regions inserted with initial text are announced by some AT/browser combos and skipped by others, so loading/unavailable states are inconsistently conveyed. Pattern issue — reported once for all locations.
fix: Keep a persistent (always-mounted, possibly empty) role="status" container per area and swap its text content, rather than mounting the live region together with its message.

verdict.reasoning: All cited instances verified: TabLoading (App.tsx:125, also the Suspense fallbacks), tide chips (:837-845), MapExplorer:1437, BirdingStats:464/:883, AtlasLayer:230, WeatherTidePanel:165-235 — every one is a conditionally-mounted element carrying role="status" together with its message, which AT announces inconsistently since the live region doesn't pre-exist its content change. Real but low-impact (loading-state awareness only; the loaded content itself is perceivable), so minor is the right severity and it's fairly batched as one pattern finding. The persistent-container fix is the standard remedy; note that for the Suspense fallbacks (TabLoading) the persistent region must live outside the Suspense boundary.

title: WCAG 2.2 forward-looking: sub-24px targets (species favicon links, combobox chevron)
description: The eBird and Birds of the World favicon links rendered next to every bird name are 14×14 px targets with a 5 px gap — under the 24×24 minimum, packed in dense table rows where the spacing exception doesn't obviously hold, and they appear hundreds of times (Life List, Breeding Codes, Checklists, Stats). The SpeciesDetail chevron (~16 px, SpeciesDetail.tsx:521) is similar. Not a WCAG 2.1 AA failure; flagged as a 2.2 delta.
fix: Grow the anchor hit area to ≥24×24 via padding on .sr-favicon-slot (visual size can stay 14px), and give the chevron button a 24px hit box.

verdict.reasoning: Same favicon facts verified independently (largely a duplicate of finding 67's part (a)): 14x14 anchor hit areas with a 5px gap (centers 19px apart < 24px, so the spacing exception fails), rendered via BirdName across Life List, Breeding Codes, Checklists, and Stats. Correctly framed as a 2.2 delta, not a 2.1 AA failure; minor stands and ACCESSIBILITY.md does not disclose it. The chevron half is weaker: the full-width 40px combobox input opens the dropdown on focus/click (SpeciesDetail.tsx onFocus handler), so the ~16px chevron plausibly meets 2.5.8's Equivalent exception.
verdict.fixNote: Padding on .sr-favicon-slot works (the anchor wraps the slot, so the anchor's hit area grows); pair it with a matching negative margin so dense table rows don't widen, and keep the img at 14px (the slot's fixed-size layout-shift guard comment in globals.css still holds if width/height become the padded total). The chevron 24px hit box is optional — it is arguably exempt under the 2.5.8 Equivalent exception since the 40px-tall input toggles the same dropdown.

title: No active color-scheme declaration; unstyled placeholders fall below AA in dark theme (~3.85:1)
description: The only color-scheme rule lives in src/index.css, which is dead code (main.tsx imports only globals.css), and no ::placeholder rule exists anywhere. In the app-controlled dark theme, UA defaults therefore stay light-scheme: Chrome's default placeholder (#757575) on the dark input surface #18181B computes to ≈3.85:1 (light theme passes ≈4.61:1); Firefox's 54%-opacity placeholder lands similarly marginal. 18 inputs use placeholders (search fields, date YYYY-MM-DD hints, API-key fields). Light-scheme scrollbars/native select popups in dark mode are a related cosmetic effect.
fix: Add `color-scheme: light` to :root and `color-scheme: dark` to [data-theme="dark"] in globals.css, plus an explicit `::placeholder { color: var(--sr-text-muted); opacity: 1 }` rule (4.83:1 light / 6.91:1 dark).

verdict.reasoning: The premise 'no ::placeholder rule exists anywhere' is false: globals.css line 1 imports Tailwind v4 (4.2.4), whose preflight sets `::placeholder { color: color-mix(in oklab, currentcolor 50%, transparent) }` (node_modules/tailwindcss/preflight.css:293), applying in Chrome/Firefox/Safari 17+ and overriding the Chrome #757575 UA default the finding's 3.85:1 math depends on. Placeholder-bearing inputs use color: var(--sr-text) on var(--sr-surface), so the actual rendered dark-theme placeholder is ~#868688 on #18181B = 4.88:1 — it PASSES AA; the genuinely marginal pair is the LIGHT theme (50% of #0F1117 on white ≈ 3.54:1), the opposite of what was filed. The missing color-scheme declaration (index.css is indeed dead code — main.tsx imports only globals.css) affects native scrollbars/select chrome only, which the finding itself concedes is cosmetic.
verdict.fixNote: Though the dark-theme claim is wrong, the suggested remediation is still worth applying for the LIGHT theme: an unlayered `::placeholder { color: var(--sr-text-muted); opacity: 1 }` in globals.css beats the @layer base preflight rule and lifts the real light-theme ~3.54:1 to 4.83:1 (6.91:1 dark), and `color-scheme: light` on :root / `color-scheme: dark` on [data-theme="dark"] fixes the native-widget chrome mismatch.

title: Chart non-text elements below 3:1: amber line in light theme, faint bar segments, stacked-segment boundaries
description: Computed non-text chart parts under 3:1 — light theme: the Audio series line --sr-graph-audio #F59E0B vs the white card = 2.15:1 (media-over-time chart; SightingsGraph media line too), --sr-chart-blue-light bar segment vs surface = 1.80:1, tier-1 fill vs surface = 2.64:1; the hand-built stacked breeding bar's adjacent segments: tier-2 vs tier-1 = 2.04:1 light / 1.50:1 dark, tier-4 vs tier-2 = 2.79:1 light / 2.20:1 dark (BirdingStats.tsx:1677-1679). Mitigations keeping this minor: every chart has a data-bearing role="img" label, tooltips, and most values are duplicated as text (legend counts, BarRow numerals).
fix: Darken light --sr-graph-audio toward #B45309 (5.02:1 — already proven in --sr-age-immature), add 1px separators between stacked-bar segments, and bump light --sr-chart-blue-light/tier-1 fills toward their 3:1 neighbors.

verdict.reasoning: Recomputed all cited non-text ratios and they match: light --sr-graph-audio #F59E0B vs white 2.15:1 (media LineChart at :1776), --sr-chart-blue-light vs white 1.80:1, tier-1 vs white 2.64:1, and the hand-built stacked breeding bar's adjacent segments at :1677-1679 (tier-2/tier-1 2.04 light / 1.50 dark; tier-4/tier-2 2.79 / 2.20). The stated mitigations are real (role="img" summaries at :557/:1266/:1755, legends, BarRow prints value+pct as text), which correctly keeps this at minor under 1.4.11's redundant-presentation allowance — the amber series line is the strongest genuine instance since the lines themselves carry the trend.
verdict.fixNote: Darkening light --sr-graph-audio toward #B45309 (5.02:1, matches light --sr-age-immature) is verified and safe. But do NOT shift the shared --sr-tier-* palette to fix the stacked-bar boundaries — those tokens drive the map atlas overlay, hatch sprites (--sr-tier-N-rgb), legend parity, and the breeding-badge dark-text-on-light-tier pairing called out in ACCESSIBILITY.md; instead add 1px var(--sr-surface) gaps between the three stacked segments at BirdingStats.tsx:1677-1679, which fixes segment distinguishability with zero blast radius.

title: Multi-series line charts differentiated by hue alone
description: The media-over-time chart draws four lines (photo/audio/video/total) distinguished only by stroke color, with a color-keyed legend — for color-blind users the photo (blue) vs video (purple) pair in particular is hard to separate. Tooltips name each series on hover and the role="img" summary covers AT users, so the information is reachable, but not glanceable. Same pattern wherever SightingsGraph's media chart overlays multiple series.
fix: Add per-series strokeDasharray patterns and/or distinct dot marker shapes to the recharts <Line> elements so series differ by more than hue.

verdict.reasoning: Lines 1775-1778 of BirdingStats.tsx render four <Line> series with dot={false}, no strokeDasharray, and only stroke color differentiating them; Vienot protan/deutan simulation collapses the photo #3B82F6 / video #8B5CF6 pair from RGB distance 88.6 to ~1-2 (same in dark theme #60A5FA/#A78BFA), confirming the confusion claim. SightingsGraph.tsx's media overlay (lines ~157-172) is likewise hue-only (its dots are same-shape circles in the series color). Hover tooltips and the role=img label keep the info reachable, so minor severity is correctly stated.
verdict.fixNote: Add per-series strokeDasharray to the four <Line>s in BirdingStats.tsx (e.g. photo solid, audio '6 3', video '2 3', total '8 3 2 3'); since dot={false} there, dashes are the practical cue. Apply the same patterns to the photo/audio/video overlay in speciesDetail/SightingsGraph.tsx (~lines 157-172). Note recharts' default Legend line icon does not render the dash pattern, so either pass a custom legend `content` or distinct `legendType` icons so the legend also differs by more than hue. Also note ACCESSIBILITY.md currently claims 'Color is never the only way information is conveyed' — update it (or fix the charts in the same change) per the CLAUDE.md rule that it must stay true.

title: Recency tier is color-alone at a glance (sighted users); the faint 'old' dot compounds it in light theme (1.64:1)
description: The fresh/mid/old recency tiers on the Nearest Targets sidebar dots and the on-map chip backgrounds are differentiated only by color for sighted users; the sr-only labels (MapExplorer.tsx:1311-1313) cover screen readers — so ACCESSIBILITY.md's specific claim about hidden labels on recency dots is TRUE — and the popup shows the tier as text ('≤7 days') plus the date, so the information is reachable by interaction. But a color-blind user scanning the list/map cannot rank targets without clicking each one, and the light-theme 'old' dot (#A8D4BB) is also only 1.64:1 against the sidebar surface (its compensating border is --sr-border at 1.27:1).
fix: Show the visible date (already computed) or a tier letter/shape next to each sidebar dot, and give the 'old' dot a ≥3:1 border (e.g. --sr-accent-strong).
