verdict.reasoning: Re-ran the WCAG math: light-theme --sr-map-target-old #A8D4BB vs the sidebar's var(--sr-surface) #FFFFFF is 1.64:1 and the dot's --sr-border #E4E4E7 border is 1.27:1 — the reported ratios are exact (the 'old' tier takes the var(--sr-border) border branch at :1310 since its text token isn't 'white'). The sidebar row (:1310-1319) shows name/location/distance but no date or tier text, and the on-map chips (TargetMarkers.tsx) are colored by tier only, so the tier IS color-alone at a glance for sighted users; the sr-only labels (:1311-1313) and the popup's '≤7 days' text + date exist as the finding accurately concedes. Minor is fair given the interaction path, and the fix is valid: --sr-accent-strong exists in both themes (globals.css:30/:131) and is 7.98:1 against the light surface.

title: 'No media' minus icon nearly invisible (1.47:1 light / 1.70:1 dark)
description: Life List media columns render a Minus icon in --sr-gray-300 (#D1D5DB) on the white row surface = 1.47:1 (dark: #3F3F46 on #18181B = 1.70:1) to mean 'no media of this type' (repeated at lines 288, 302, 316, 331). The meaning ('zero') is inferable from the absence of a count link, which is why this is minor rather than moderate, but the chosen glyph as drawn fails non-text contrast in both themes.
fix: Use --sr-text-disabled or --sr-border-medium darkened to ≥3:1, or render a plain '—' in --sr-text-muted (which also gives AT users something to announce).

verdict.reasoning: Recomputed independently: --sr-gray-300 on --sr-surface is #D1D5DB/#FFFFFF = 1.47:1 light and #3F3F46/#18181B = 1.70:1 dark — exactly as reported, at lines 288/302/316/331, well under the 3:1 of SC 1.4.11. Minor is the right severity since the absent count link redundantly conveys 'zero'. Not covered by ACCESSIBILITY.md's lone known exception (chart-bar percentage labels).
verdict.fixNote: Two of the finding's three suggested tokens fail its own 3:1 target: --sr-text-disabled computes to 2.56:1 light / 2.29:1 dark, and --sr-border-medium to 1.73:1 / 1.70:1 (its dark value IS #3F3F46, the currently-failing color). Use the third option only: color the glyph var(--sr-text-muted) (#71717A light = 4.83:1, #A1A1AA dark = 6.91:1; token already defined in both themes), either keeping the <Minus> icon or rendering a text em dash — the text variant additionally gives screen readers something to announce.

title: Life List species column is <td>, not a row header, unlike the Breeding Codes table
description: BreedingCodeTable.tsx:174 correctly marks the species name cell <th scope="row">, but LifeListTable.tsx:267 uses a plain <td>. The Photo/Audio/Video count cells contain links whose only content is a bare number (e.g. "3"), so when navigating by cell or link, SRs that announce row headers would give the species context automatically in the Breeding table but not here. Column-header context still works, so impact is small.
fix: Change the species cell to <th scope="row" style={{...textAlign:'left'}}> to match BreedingCodeTable.tsx:174.

verdict.reasoning: Verified both halves: LifeListTable.tsx:267 is a plain <td> while BreedingCodeTable.tsx:174 uses <th scope="row"> (with a comment explaining the textAlign reset), so the inconsistency is real and the bare-number link cells (e.g. "3") genuinely benefit from row-header semantics. Column headers still provide context, so this sits at the best-practice edge of 1.3.1; minor is the correct severity and the framing is honest, not pedantic.
verdict.fixNote: Match BreedingCodeTable.tsx:174-187 fully: <th scope="row" style={{ padding: '9px 14px', verticalAlign: 'middle', textAlign: 'left', fontWeight: 'normal' }}>. The fontWeight: 'normal' reset (present in BreedingCodeTable at line 186 but omitted from the finding's snippet) matters because .sr-birdname-sci sets no font-weight, so the italic scientific-name line would otherwise inherit the th bold default.

title: Southern-hemisphere moon emoji mirroring makes screen readers announce the wrong phase
description: The moon-phase emoji is the ONLY carrier of moon-phase information in night weather blocks (no adjacent text line — the condition emoji, by contrast, is followed by the textual condition on the next line). For northern latitudes this is acceptable: SRs read Unicode emoji names ("waxing gibbous moon"), which match the phase. But MOON_SOUTH deliberately swaps to the visually-mirrored emoji for lat < 0, so a southern-hemisphere waxing crescent is rendered as 🌘 whose Unicode name is "waning crescent moon" — a SR (and anyone hovering for the character name) hears the opposite phase. Constrained by the paste-into-eBird output format, so an in-app-only fix is appropriate.
fix: Where the formatted block is displayed in-app (the <pre> on the Weather tab and WeatherTidePanel), wrap the header emoji run in a span with an aria-label giving the true phase name (e.g. "cloudy, waxing crescent moon"), or append the phase as text in the in-app rendering only.

verdict.reasoning: weatherFormatter.ts:93-102 swaps to mirrored emoji for lat<0, so all six asymmetric phases carry the opposite phase's Unicode name (verified: southern waxing crescent emits 🌘 'waning crescent moon'); the emoji is the block's only phase carrier (formatWeatherBody emits `${emoji}${moon}` with no phase text line) and renders as raw text in the Weather tab <pre> (App.tsx:827) and WeatherTidePanel's MonoBlock, where SRs announce it by character name. ACCESSIBILITY.md does not disclose this — it actually claims icon-only info carries hidden text labels. Minor is fair: narrow trigger (southern hemisphere + night checklist + SR) but the announced info is actively wrong, a genuine 1.1.1 failure.
verdict.fixNote: In the in-app renderings only (App.tsx Weather-tab <pre> ~line 811 and WeatherTidePanel's MonoBlock), split off the header line and wrap the emoji run in <span role="img" aria-label="..."> — a bare span aria-label is not reliably honored by SRs without role="img". Derive the true phase name by exporting it from weatherFormatter.ts (e.g. a moonPhaseName(unixTs) beside moonPhaseEmoji, or reverse-lookup the rendered emoji's index in MOON_SOUTH when lat < 0; northern emoji names are already correct). Do NOT change formatWeatherBody's output string — it is byte-locked with backend/formatters/weather.py and the commentBlocks.ts stripper anchors on the unspaced contiguous emoji run.

title: Settings radiogroups use role=radio without the expected arrow-key behavior
wcag: 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (ARIA radiogroup pattern) AA
description: The Color theme (:119), Text size (:519), and Date format (:586) groups are role="radiogroup" containing role="radio" buttons that are all tabIndex={0}. Screen readers announce them as radio buttons (e.g. "radio, 1 of 4") and instruct arrow-key navigation, but arrow keys do nothing and unchecked radios remain in the Tab order — behavior that contradicts the announced role. Users can still operate everything with Tab+Enter, so impact is confusion rather than blockage.
fix: Either implement the radiogroup pattern (roving tabindex + ArrowLeft/Right to move checked state) or downgrade to the house pattern used elsewhere: plain buttons with aria-pressed inside role="group" aria-label.

verdict.reasoning: Same verified facts as index 37: three role=radiogroup/role=radio groups (119, 519, 586) with all-tabIndex={0} buttons, no arrow-key handling, no roving tabindex, so SR-announced radio semantics contradict actual behavior while Tab+Enter still works. The finding correctly scopes impact to confusion rather than blockage, so minor is appropriate (note 4.1.2 is Level A, not AA as labeled — immaterial). The suggested downgrade to the house aria-pressed pattern is validated (SortSeg at Checklists.tsx:67, aria-pressed used across BreedingCodeList and others).

title: Species selector dropdown toggle chevron is a mouse-only <span>
description: The chevron that opens/closes the species combobox list is a <span onClick> with no role, name, or tab stop. Keyboard users are not blocked (the input opens the listbox on focus and Escape closes it), but a pointer-AT or switch user targeting the visible affordance gets a dead control, and it is invisible to screen readers.
fix: Either mark it aria-hidden="true" (treating it as decorative since the input itself toggles the list), or make it a real <button tabIndex={-1} aria-label="Toggle species list"> per the ARIA combobox pattern.

verdict.reasoning: Same element as finding 73 (SpeciesDetail.tsx:521-531) viewed through 2.1.1: the visible toggle affordance is a mouse-only <span> — dead for switch/voice users targeting it, invisible to SR — though a full keyboard path exists through the input itself, so minor is the right severity. Confirmed in current code; no aria-hidden present. This is a duplicate of finding 73 and should be merged with it; the fix options given are both acceptable, with the tabIndex={-1} named button being the APG-preferred one.

title: WCAG 2.2 forward-looking: several form controls are under the 24px minimum target size
description: Forward-looking 2.2 delta only. The atlas overlay role="switch" buttons are 38x22px (MapExplorer.tsx:726, :759, :788 — 22px tall, under the 24px minimum), and several zero-padding text buttons are ~16-18px tall: the API-key Show/Hide button (Settings.tsx:363-373, padding 0, 0.75rem text), the 'Clear filter' underline buttons (LifeList.tsx:694-703, Checklists.tsx:685-690, SpeciesDetail.tsx:658-667), and the 'Go to Settings →' banner buttons (App.tsx:611-619, padding 0). Most currently escape 2.5.8 via the spacing exception (no adjacent target within 24px), but that is fragile under layout changes and the small targets are already hard for motor-impaired users under 2.1 best practice.
fix: Bump the switch buttons to at least 24px tall (e.g. 44x24 track) and give the zero-padding text buttons enough padding (or min-height: 24px with negative-margin compensation) to reach a 24x24 hit area.

verdict.reasoning: All cited controls verified: the three hand-rolled role=switch buttons are 38x22 (MapExplorer.tsx:726, :759, :788 — 22px tall, under 24), and the padding-0 text buttons exist as described in Settings.tsx:363-373 (Show/Hide), LifeList.tsx:694-703 / Checklists.tsx:685-690 / SpeciesDetail.tsx:658-667 (Clear filter), and App.tsx:611-619 (Go to Settings), all at 0.75rem with no padding (~17px hit height). The finding honestly frames itself as a forward-looking WCAG 2.2 delta and acknowledges the spacing exception currently covers most of them, so minor is the right severity.
verdict.fixNote: The codebase already has a shared ui/ToggleSwitch.tsx (a 30px-tall role=switch button with the label inside) — prefer migrating the three inline atlas switches to it, or if the label-left/switch-right layout must stay, bump the bare track to >=24px tall (e.g. 44x24). For the zero-padding text buttons, padding (or min-height 24 with negative-margin compensation) as originally suggested is fine.

title: WCAG 2.2: 12px icon-only eBird link in Nearest Unvisited Hotspots rows is below Target Size minimum
description: The external eBird link in each 'Nearest Unvisited Hotspots' row is an inline-flex anchor whose only content is a 12px ExternalLink icon with no padding, giving a ~12-14px hit target packed between the location-name button and the distance text — below the 24x24 CSS px minimum of WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 and a genuinely hard touch/low-motor target. (For comparison, the equivalent crosshair locate buttons at :1326-1330 are 26x26 and pass.)
fix: Give the anchor a fixed 24x24 (or 26x26 to match the crosshair buttons) box with centered icon, e.g. width/height 24 + justifyContent center.

verdict.reasoning: Verified at MapExplorer.tsx:1108-1118: the anchor is inline-flex with no padding around an ExternalLink size={12} icon, giving a ~12px hit target sitting 6px from the flex:1 location-name button on one side and the distance text on the other — under 2.5.8's 24px minimum, and the 6px gap means the spacing exception does not rescue it (the 24px circles of the anchor and the adjacent ~15px-tall name button intersect). The 26x26 crosshair comparison at :1326-1330 checks out. Fairly flagged as a forward-looking 2.2 item; minor is right and the suggested fixed 24x24/26x26 centered box matches the existing crosshair-button pattern.

title: Boot spinner's reduced-motion fallback slows the spin to 2s instead of stopping it
wcag: 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions (AAA, honored as policy per ACCESSIBILITY.md)
description: The pre-React boot screen spinner (.sr-boot-spin, an infinite 0.7s rotation) carries its own inline prefers-reduced-motion rule that merely slows the rotation to 2s per revolution rather than stopping it. This deliberately diverges from the published ACCESSIBILITY.md claim that 'loading spinners ... are reduced to near-instant.' In a production build the gap is neutralized: Vite injects the bundled globals.css as a render-blocking <link>, and its document-wide `* { animation-duration: 0.001ms !important; animation-iteration-count: 1 !important }` RM block (globals.css:588-594) overrides the inline rule at first paint (author !important beats normal declarations), freezing the spinner. The slow spin therefore only manifests in dev mode (JS-injected styles arrive after first paint) or if the bundled stylesheet fails to load. No WCAG AA failure: the boot screen has no parallel content and the spinner is a loading-phase progress indicator (2.2.2 exception), but it is the one motion source not strictly covered by the kill, and it makes the blanket 'near-instant' statement technically inaccurate for the pre-CSS window.
fix: Either change the inline rule to `.sr-boot-spin { animation: none; }` (the frozen ring still communicates loading via the role="status" aria-label "Loading SnowRaven" on line 28), or — if the slow rotation is a deliberate 'gentle feedback' choice — note that one exception in ACCESSIBILITY.md's Reduced Motion section so the published claim stays exactly true.

verdict.reasoning: Code claims verify (index.html:23 slows to 2s; globals.css:588-594 has the !important kill), but I confirmed the built dist/index.html loads the bundled CSS as render-blocking <link>s in <head>, so first paint cannot occur before the document-wide reduced-motion kill applies — no RM user of any shipped build (Tauri or web/Pi) ever sees the 2s spin. The ACCESSIBILITY.md 'near-instant' claim is therefore exactly true as experienced, and the residual behavior exists only in dev mode or total-CSS-failure scenarios, neither user-facing. Technically-true but zero real user impact; the finding itself documents its own neutralization.

title: Four inline `animation: 'spin …'` styles in MapExplorer bypass the .spin class convention
wcag: 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions (policy per ACCESSIBILITY.md) — regression-risk only, no current failure
description: MapExplorer.tsx applies the spinner keyframes via inline style objects instead of the shared `.spin` class at four sites: line 657 (map loading chip, 'spin 1s linear infinite'), line 682 ('Locating…' spinner, 'spin 0.7s linear infinite'), line 1003 and line 1224 (hotspots / media-targets 'Finding…' spinners, 'spin 1s linear infinite'). There is NO current user impact: the reduced-motion kill in globals.css:588-594 uses a universal `*` selector with `!important` longhands, and author !important declarations override inline styles, so these spinners are correctly frozen for reduced-motion users today. The risk is silent regression: these are the only animations in the codebase that escape the `.spin` class, so any future refactor that scopes the RM block to classes (e.g. `.spin { animation: none }`) instead of `*` would leave these four spinning for reduced-motion users with nothing failing visibly. Reported once; all four locations listed here.
fix: Replace the inline `animation:` declarations with `className="spin"` at MapExplorer.tsx lines 657, 682, 1003, and 1224 (matching every other spinner in the app), so all spinner motion flows through the one class the reduced-motion CSS is built around.

verdict.reasoning: All four inline animation:'spin' sites exist as cited and a repo-wide grep confirms they are the only spinners bypassing the .spin class (line 1438 of the same file uses it). The reduced-motion block (globals.css:588-594) is `*` + !important longhands, which does override inline styles, so the finding's no-current-failure, regression-risk-only framing is accurate and fairly flagged against the published reduced-motion commitment in ACCESSIBILITY.md.
verdict.fixNote: Suggested fix is correct and convention-aligned. One caveat: .spin runs at 0.7s while lines 657/1003/1224 use 1s, so adopting the class slightly speeds those three spinners — cosmetic and consistent with the rest of the app; line 682 already matches 0.7s.

title: Statistics map rank-pin numerals are fixed 10px SVG text — only text in the app that ignores the Text Size control
description: RankIcon renders a fixed 24×24 SVG with `fontSize="10"` for the rank numbers on the Statistics geographic map pins (BirdingStats.tsx:865, 871). The numeral does not scale with the Text Size control or OS text size. Mitigations: it is map content (markers on a map get latitude under 1.4.10/1.4.4), and the same ranking is available as scalable text in the "Top locations by checklists/species" lists directly below (BirdingStats.tsx:906, 921). Reported as polish, plus a note: the icon fills are hardcoded hex (`#2D8653`, `#3B82F6`, echoed in the legend swatches at BirdingStats.tsx:888/892 and the popup gray `#71717A` at :876), which violates the project's own --sr-* token rule.
fix: Size the SVG in em (width/height '1.5em') so the pin and numeral track the root scale, or accept as map content and document it; swap the hardcoded hexes for var(--sr-*) tokens while there.

verdict.reasoning: RankIcon (statsPrimitives.tsx:92-101) is exactly as described — fixed 24x24 SVG with fontSize="10" numerals used as map Markers at BirdingStats.tsx:865/871, and a grep confirms it is the only SVG <text> in the app, so the numerals are the one text surface that ignores the Text Size control. The stated mitigations hold (the identical ranks render as scalable HTML text in the lists at BirdingStats.tsx:904-925, and map markers get 1.4.10/1.4.4 latitude), so minor/polish is the right severity; the bundled token complaint is also real — #2D8653/#3B82F6/#71717A are hardcoded against CLAUDE.md's explicit 'no hardcoded hex in component files' rule. The popup gray is worse than stylistic: the MapLibre popup background is themed (var(--sr-surface) = #18181B dark), and I computed #71717A on it at 3.67:1, below AA, while var(--sr-text-muted) is #A1A1AA in dark theme precisely for this.
verdict.fixNote: Em-sizing the SVG works (DOM markers inherit the scaled root font-size; note pins double in footprint at 200% and overlap more — acceptable). But do NOT blind-swap the pin fills to var(--sr-accent)/var(--sr-graph-photo): those tokens lighten in dark theme (#34D399/#60A5FA) and the white numeral would drop well below AA, while the pins sit on theme-independent map tiles where the current dark fills are correct in both themes — mint dedicated --sr-rank-pin-circle/--sr-rank-pin-square tokens in BOTH :root and [data-theme=dark] (same dark values in each is fine) and use them for both RankIcon and the legend swatches at BirdingStats.tsx:888/892. The popup gray at :876 should become var(--sr-text-muted) — that one is a real dark-theme AA fix (3.67:1 today), not just hygiene.

title: Map Explorer filters accordion clamps to maxHeight 600px with overflow:hidden — fails closed if content ever exceeds it
description: The collapsible filter panel animates via `maxHeight: filterOpen ? 600 : 0` with `overflow: 'hidden'`. Measuring the current contents (species select, date range, county, breeding seg-control, media select ≈300px at 100%; ≈450-500px at 200% with seg-control wrapping), there is headroom today, so this is not a present-day failure. But the construction fails silently: any future filter addition, or further text growth, pushes the bottom controls (the Media select) past 600px where they are clipped and unreachable with no scrollbar — the classic animated-max-height trap. Flagged so it isn't extended blindly.
fix: Animate with `grid-template-rows: 0fr/1fr` + `min-height: 0` (no hard cap), or raise the open clamp to a generous `maxHeight: 'none'` after the transition ends, keeping 600px only as the transition target.

verdict.reasoning: Line 848 is exactly `maxHeight: filterOpen ? 600 : 0` with overflow:hidden and no scrollbar path; clipped content would be unreachable since the clamped div sits inside the sidebar scroll container. I re-measured at 200% text scale: selects/inputs/SegControl are fixed-height px and only rem labels grow, so contents land ~420-500px — under the clamp, confirming no present-day 1.4.4 failure exactly as the finding states. Fairly-flagged fail-closed construction on a panel that conditionally gains filters (County, Media), kept at minor as forward-looking only.
verdict.fixNote: Both suggested options work; the grid-template-rows 0fr/1fr technique requires `min-height: 0` plus `overflow: hidden` on the inner row and is supported in WKWebView (Safari 16+) and WebView2, so it is safe for the desktop targets. The transitionend→maxHeight:'none' variant is the smaller diff for this inline-styled component.

title: Comparer media/side-header cells fixed at 132px
description: The per-row media/count cell (`width: 132, flexShrink: 0`, ChecklistComparer.tsx:74) and its matching SideHeader (`width: 132`, :506) are fixed pixel widths holding 0.75rem text and badges. At 200% the cell contents (count + breeding-code badge + media badges) exceed 132px and push into the species-name column. Same family as the Statistics fixed-px finding but a separate file/owner, listed for completeness.
fix: Use a rem width (e.g. '9rem') or `minWidth` so the cell grows with its text; keep header and cell sharing one constant.

verdict.reasoning: Verified width: 132/flexShrink: 0 at line 74, the matching SideHeader 132 at line 506, plus a fixed 34px count box at line 88; lib/textScale.ts scales only rem text (--sr-text-scale up to 2x), so at 200% the rem-sized badge text outgrows the px boxes and a badge-dense row overflows or clips. Cannot be refuted via browser zoom: ACCESSIBILITY.md explicitly claims SC 1.4.4 conformance through the in-app control because the desktop app has no browser zoom, and its only zoom disclosure (horizontal scroll for tables/maps under 1.4.10) does not cover this. Minor is the right severity — localized overlap on the densest rows of one tab.
verdict.fixNote: Prefer a shared rem-width constant (e.g. const SIDE_CELL_WIDTH = '9rem') used by both SideCell and SideHeader over minWidth — minWidth would let per-row cell widths diverge and break the A/B count alignment the fixed width exists for (per the code comment 'Fixed width so counts line up'). Also convert the inner count box at line 88 from width: 34 to a rem value (e.g. '2.25rem'), since it clips 3-digit counts at 200% independently of the cell width.

title: Mobile filter-panel focus trap snapshots focusables once at open — focus can escape after content inside the panel changes
wcag: 2.4.3 Focus Order A (published claim: 'keeps it there while open')
description: The statement says opening the Map Explorer filter panel 'moves focus into the panel and keeps it there while open' — and the trap (MapExplorer.tsx:187-221) does focus the first element, wrap Tab/Shift+Tab, and return focus on Escape. However `focusable` is queried once when the panel opens; the wrap comparison uses the stale `first`/`last` references. The panel's content is dynamic (the Filters accordion expands, async hotspot/target fetches append in-view list rows after the snapshot's last element), so after such a change, Tab from the true last element no longer matches `last` and focus walks out of the overlay onto the map content behind the backdrop. Edge case, but it makes the 'keeps it there' claim conditionally false.
fix: Re-query the focusable list inside the keydown handler (or on each Tab press) instead of capturing first/last at open time.

verdict.reasoning: Verified: the trap (lines 187-221, deps [sidebarOpen]) snapshots focusables once and wraps against captured first/last, while the sidebar's content is dynamic — the in-view marker lists and the async 'Find hotspots'/targets search results all render inside sidebarRef, so Tab from a newly-appended true-last element escapes the overlay, contradicting the ACCESSIBILITY.md 'keeps it there while open' claim. One correction: the Filters accordion expansion does NOT change the focusable set (its collapsed content stays in the DOM, merely clipped by maxHeight:0, and is already in the snapshot); the async list mutations are the real escape path. Edge case on mobile only, so minor is right; ACCESSIBILITY.md states the opposite, which is a claim, not a disclosure.
verdict.fixNote: Re-query `sidebar.querySelectorAll(...)` inside handleKeyDown on each Tab press and derive first/last from the live list. While there, filter to visible elements (e.g. `el.offsetParent !== null`) so the controls clipped inside the collapsed Filters accordion (maxHeight:0, overflow:hidden — still tabbable today) stop being invisible tab stops.
